subject.title: github-copilot: legacy OAuth token refresh sends bearer credential to unvalidated enterpriseUrl domain

question: Should maintainers treat this public legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth refresh report as an immediate security fix in OpenClaw, and what disclosure/rotation handling should accompany the code change?
rationale: The source-level fix appears narrow, but the reported behavior can send bearer refresh credentials to an attacker-controlled host and the affected shape exists in the latest release, so automation should not decide the security handling alone.

options.title: Patch legacy refresh under security review
options.body: Keep this issue open, assign a security-reviewed fix that reuses the existing allowlist for legacy refresh and migration/persisted-state tests, and decide any disclosure or credential-rotation note separately.

options.title: Move to private advisory handling
options.body: Pause public repair automation and transfer the discussion to the repository security process if maintainers want coordinated disclosure before patch details expand.

options.title: Accept legacy-only risk
options.body: Document that legacy OAuth `enterpriseUrl` state is unsupported and close without code only if maintainers explicitly accept the shipped credential-host risk.

recommendation.title: Patch legacy refresh under security review
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, assign a security-reviewed fix that reuses the existing allowlist for legacy refresh and migration/persisted-state tests, and decide any disclosure or credential-rotation note separately.
